Technical requirements / goals:
- Workloads: chat (session state + function calls), embeddings for semantic search, reranking for recommendations, on-demand summarization.
- Latency targets: 95p < 350ms for short-chat (<=256 tokens), p99 < 700ms for mixed-length; throughput target ~120 req/s sustained at peak.
- Cost sensitivity: wants 20-30% lower token cost than current provider when on Dedicated.
- Model preferences: open model variants acceptable; prefer deterministic rollout from hosted -> dedicated with pinning.
- Routing/fallback: must support region-aware routing (NA/EU), auto-fallback to smaller model variants under contention.

Migration specifics (compatibility focus):
- "Compatibility layer" objective: minimize app changes. Customer currently uses vendor X SDK with streaming+function-calls. Wants a thin shim so frontend calls remain identical.
- Key parity concerns: stop sequences/stop-token behavior, temperature sampling differences, tokenizer discrepancies causing subtle prompt/response drift.
- Function-calling: map vendor X function-calling schema to Redwood's function call metadata. Demo showed minimal SDK changes for server-side, frontend only needs endpoint switch.
- Streaming: chunk sizes and chunk-arrival timing differ; customer worried about UI flicker/regression. SE recommended adjusting stream buffer (client) and Redwood streaming config to mimic vendor X pacing.

POC results and findings:
- Eval harness: 1.2k prompt set with gold labels + biz-critical prompts (billing language, policy-safe wording).
- Parity: ~92% syntactic parity on short responses; 7% of prompts produced altered semantics (edge-case factuality/regression).
- Notable regressions: reranker score order differences for 3 important queries — impacted UI ranking. Filed RW-1542.
- Tokenization: observed ~3% token count variance causing cost delta on long docs.
- Latency: Hosted API met 95p target for chat at low load; at higher concurrency observed increased tail latency (investigating batching config).
